name: Hertsmere

licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: the council says it has not used this power. Mandatory licensing applies to HMOs with five or more people from two or more households. An Article 4 direction for Potters Bar (2026) means converting a home to a small HMO there needs planning permission, and revised HMO amenity standards apply from 25 November 2026.
licensing.fee: £1,306 to renew an HMO licence for up to five people, plus £105 for each extra person

housing: Hertsmere lies just north of London, made up of Borehamwood, Potters Bar, Bushey, Radlett and green belt villages. Borehamwood's large post-war estates were built for families moving out of London, and many former council homes there are now privately let, alongside newer flats near the film studios. Bushey, Radlett and Potters Bar have interwar and Edwardian family houses and blocks of flats, with some very large detached homes. Prices and rents are high, and private renting grew faster than across the East of England between 2011 and 2021.
checkinTips: Post-war estate houses and maisonettes in Borehamwood: record the boiler, windows and doors, and communal areas, bin stores and garages.
Flats in Borehamwood, Bushey and Potters Bar town centres: note fob and key counts, parking spaces and any lift or communal heating.
Large detached houses in Radlett and Bushey Heath: photograph gardens, gates, alarm systems and garden equipment left in place.
Interwar semis in Potters Bar: record original features, replacement windows, garages and extensions.
Shared homes in Potters Bar: an Article 4 direction applies to new small HMOs there, so note the licence or planning position and photograph each room's lock and furniture.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Hertsmere Borough Council's private sector housing team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
